Entire's CLI is the source of truth for its own usage. Do not guess flags or
subcommands — read them from this command. You are already inside the repo:
entire auto-detects it from the git origin remote, so never ask the user for the
repo name. Pass --repo only to target a DIFFERENT repo.

Current repo: gh/entireio/cli  (auto-detected from origin; pass --repo only for a DIFFERENT repo)

When to use entire:
  activity     Show your activity overview
  agent        Manage agent integrations (add, remove, list)
  api          Make an authenticated request to an Entire API and print the response
  auth         Manage authentication
  blame        Show which lines came from Entire checkpoints
  checkpoint   Inspect and search checkpoints
  clean        Clean up Entire session data
  configure    Update Entire settings in the current repository
  disable      Disable Entire in current repository
  dispatch     Generate a dispatch summarizing recent agent work
  doctor       Diagnose and fix session issues
  enable       Enable Entire in current repository
  experts      Rank agent provenance for code scopes
  grant        Manage Entire access grants and org membership
  import       Import pre-existing agent history into Entire (experimental)
  investigate  Run a multi-agent investigation against the current branch
  labs         Explore experimental Entire workflows
  login        Log in to Entire
  logout       Log out of Entire
  org          Manage Entire organizations
  plugin       Manage Entire plugins (install, list, remove)
  project      Manage Entire projects
  recap        Summarize recent checkpoint activity
  repo         Manage Entire repositories
  review       Run a multi-agent review against the current branch
  runner       Set up and tune trail runners for this repository
  search       Search checkpoints, commits, and sessions using semantic and keyword matching
  session      Manage agent sessions tracked by Entire
  status       Show Entire status
  tokens       Analyze token usage across sessions and checkpoints
  trail        Manage trails for your branches
  version      Show build information
  why          Show why a line exists

Drill in for exact, currently-installed flags:  entire agent-help <command>  (e.g. entire agent-help trail)
Add --json for structured output.

entire enable — Enable Entire in current repository
Enable Entire with session tracking for your AI agent workflows.

If Entire is not yet configured, this runs the full configuration flow.
If Entire is already configured but disabled, this re-enables it.

If the current directory is not a git repository, Entire can initialize one
for you and (optionally) create a matching GitHub repository via the gh CLI.

Current repo: gh/entireio/cli  (auto-detected from origin; pass --repo only for a DIFFERENT repo)

Flags:
      --absolute-git-hook-path               Embed full binary path in git hooks (for GUI git clients that don't source shell profiles)
      --agent string                         Agent to set up hooks for (e.g., claude-code, codex, copilot-cli, cursor, factoryai-droid, gemini, opencode, pi; external agents on $PATH are also available). Enables non-interactive mode.
      --agent-help-skill entire agent-help   Install the stable Entire agent-help skill (points agents at entire agent-help) for selected agent(s)
      --checkpoint-backend string            Checkpoint storage backend: refs (one git ref per checkpoint; recommended) or branch (shared entire/checkpoints/v1 branch)
      --checkpoint-remote string             Checkpoint remote in provider:owner/repo format (e.g., github:org/checkpoints-repo)
  -f, --force                                Force reinstall hooks (removes existing Entire hooks first)
      --init-repo                            If not a git repo, initialize one non-interactively
      --initial-commit-message string        Commit message for the initial commit when bootstrapping a new repo
      --local                                Write settings to .entire/settings.local.json instead of .entire/settings.json
      --no-github                            Initialize local git repo only; skip creating a GitHub remote
      --no-init-repo                         If not a git repo, exit instead of prompting to initialize one
      --project                              Write settings to .entire/settings.json even if it already exists
      --push                                 When bootstrapping a new repo, push the initial commit to the created GitHub remote (implies creating the remote; without it the repo is created but not pushed)
      --repo-name string                     GitHub repository name for the new repo (used when bootstrapping)
      --repo-owner string                    GitHub user or organization login for the new repo
      --repo-visibility string               GitHub repository visibility: public, private, or internal
      --search-skill                         Install the optional Entire search skill for selected agent(s)
      --skip-initial-commit                  Don't create the initial commit when bootstrapping a new repo
      --skip-push-sessions                   Disable automatic pushing of session logs on git push
      --telemetry                            Enable anonymous usage analytics (default true)
  -y, --yes                                  Accept all defaults without prompting (in a non-repo directory: init git, create private GitHub repo, commit, and push; then enable all agents and accept telemetry)

# `entire enable`: Complete Potential Interactive Flow and Output

```text
ENTIRE ENABLE — COMPLETE POTENTIAL INTERACTIVE FLOW
===================================================

Scope
-----
This is a source-derived map of the potential prompts, decisions, status lines,
conditional notes, and completion output reachable from `entire enable`.

Primary implementation sources:
  cmd/entire/cli/setup.go
  cmd/entire/cli/setup_github.go
  cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint_backend.go
  cmd/entire/cli/setup_import.go
  cmd/entire/cli/setup_search_skill.go
  cmd/entire/cli/setup_agent_help_skill.go
  cmd/entire/cli/strategy/hook_managers.go

Notation used below:
  <VALUE>               Dynamic value.
  [default]             Preselected/default answer.
  [conditional]         Printed or prompted only when the stated condition holds.
  ├─ / └─               Mutually exclusive branches.
  AGENT                  Any registered built-in or external agent with hook support.
  CONFIG                 .entire/settings.json or .entire/settings.local.json.
  REPO_PATH              Absolute path to the current directory.
  OWNER/REPO             Selected GitHub owner and repository name.

The normal TUI is rendered by huh and may redraw lines while the user moves the
cursor. The stable titles, descriptions, labels, defaults, and final output are
listed here. With ACCESSIBLE set, the same forms render as numbered questions or
[Y/n] / [y/N] confirmations and usually omit descriptions.


TOP-LEVEL ROUTING
=================

$ entire enable

0. Validate command state and flags.

   0.1 Validate --checkpoint-backend before performing bootstrap or installing
       hooks.

       Accepted user-facing values:
         refs
         branch

       Canonical values also accepted, case-insensitively:
         git-refs
         git-branch

       Invalid value:
         Error: invalid --checkpoint-backend: <VALIDATION_ERROR>

   0.2 If both settings-scope flags are supplied:

         Error: cannot specify both --project and --local

   0.3 Discover external agents before resolving --agent or building an agent
       picker. Any external agent found on PATH may therefore appear beside the
       built-in options shown later.

   0.4 If --agent was explicitly supplied with no value:

         Missing agent name. Available agents:

           claude-code    (default)
           codex
           copilot-cli
           cursor
           factoryai-droid
           gemini
           opencode
           pi
           <EXTERNAL_AGENT_NAME>

         Usage: entire enable --agent <agent-name>

   0.5 If --agent <NAME> does not resolve:

         Unknown agent "<NAME>". Available agents:

           claude-code    (default)
           codex
           copilot-cli
           cursor
           factoryai-droid
           gemini
           opencode
           pi
           <EXTERNAL_AGENT_NAME>

         Usage: entire enable --agent <agent-name>

1. Determine whether the current directory is already a git repository.

   ├─ YES: skip the entire git/GitHub bootstrap section and continue at
   │       "REPOSITORY SETUP ROUTING".
   │
   └─ NO: enter "NON-GIT DIRECTORY BOOTSTRAP".


NON-GIT DIRECTORY BOOTSTRAP
===========================

This section is reachable only when the current directory is not inside a git
worktree. It runs before agent selection and Entire configuration.

A. Bare interactive bootstrap: one merged setup picker
-------------------------------------------------------

Condition:
  - interactive prompting is available; and
  - none of these choices was already supplied by flags:
      --yes
      --init-repo
      --no-init-repo
      --no-github
      --repo-name
      --repo-owner
      --repo-visibility
      --push
      --initial-commit-message
      --skip-initial-commit

Prompt:

  ? No git repository in "<REPO_PATH>". Set one up?

    > Yes, with one initial commit (recommended)                 [default]
      Yes, plus a private GitHub repository (pushed)             [only when gh is installed and authenticated]
      Yes, customize...
      No

A1. Select "No"
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

No filesystem mutation occurs. Output:

  Not a git repository. Please run 'entire enable' from within a git repository, or pass --init-repo to initialize one here.

A Ctrl+C at this merged picker is treated like selecting "No" and also leaves
the folder untouched.

A2. Select "Yes, with one initial commit (recommended)"
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

The local-only preset means:
  - initialize git;
  - do not create a GitHub repository;
  - create one initial commit with message "Initial commit";
  - do not ask the custom GitHub/commit/push questions.

Output:

  Setting up git repository
    ✓ Initialized empty git repository

If git identity is already configured, no identity prompt appears.
If identity is missing but can be sourced from authenticated gh:

    Using git identity: <NAME> <<EMAIL>>

If one or both identity fields are still missing, show the applicable input
field or fields:

  ? Git user.name
    <USER_INPUT>

  ? Git user.email
    <USER_INPUT>

Both values are required. Empty submission eventually fails with:

  Error: git user.name and user.email are both required

After identity resolution, continue with:

  Enabling Entire

Then run the fresh-repository Entire wizard described later. Its normal final
"Ready." line is suppressed because bootstrap owns the final summary.

After Entire setup succeeds:

  Finalizing
    ✓ Created initial commit

Or, if no files exist to commit:

  Finalizing
    ✓ Nothing to commit — the folder has no files yet

Then:

  Done.

A3. Select "Yes, plus a private GitHub repository (pushed)"
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

This option appears only when gh is installed and authenticated. The preset
means:
  - initialize git;
  - resolve the current GitHub user automatically;
  - derive the repository name from the folder automatically;
  - create a private GitHub repository;
  - create one initial commit with message "Initial commit";
  - push the initial commit;
  - skip the granular owner/name/visibility/commit/push prompts.

Output begins:

  Setting up git repository
    ✓ Initialized empty git repository
    Using GitHub owner: <CURRENT_GITHUB_USER>

Identity output, when sourced from gh:

    Using git identity: <NAME> <<EMAIL>>

If gh cannot supply both identity fields, the applicable identity inputs are
shown:

  ? Git user.name
    <USER_INPUT>

  ? Git user.email
    <USER_INPUT>

Then:

  Enabling Entire

After the fresh-repository Entire wizard succeeds:

  Publishing to GitHub
    ✓ Created initial commit
    ✓ Created <OWNER/REPO> (private)
      https://github.com/<OWNER/REPO>
    ✓ Pushed initial commit to origin

  Done.

If the folder still has nothing to commit:

  Publishing to GitHub
    ✓ Nothing to commit — the folder has no files yet
    ✓ Created <OWNER/REPO> (private)
      https://github.com/<OWNER/REPO>

  Done.

No push occurs when no commit was created.

A4. Select "Yes, customize..."
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

Output first:

  Setting up git repository
    ✓ Initialized empty git repository

Then enter the granular custom branch described under section C.


B. Granular initialization consent
----------------------------------

The merged picker is skipped when a bootstrap-related flag already expresses a
partial decision. Depending on flags, initialization is accepted, declined, or
prompted separately.

B1. --init-repo or --yes
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

Initialization is accepted without a prompt.

B2. --no-init-repo
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

Initialization is declined without a prompt. Output:

  Not a git repository. Please run 'entire enable' from within a git repository, or pass --init-repo to initialize one here.

B3. A granular flag was supplied, but init consent was not
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

Prompt, default No:

  ? Warning: Not a git repository. Initialize a new one in "<REPO_PATH>"?

      Yes
    > No                                                        [default]

If No or Ctrl+C:

  Not a git repository. Please run 'entire enable' from within a git repository, or pass --init-repo to initialize one here.

If Yes:

  Setting up git repository
    ✓ Initialized empty git repository

Then continue through the custom choices that were not already answered by
flags.


C. Custom bootstrap: whether to create a GitHub repository
----------------------------------------------------------

C1. --no-github or the local preset
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

Do not prompt and do not create a remote.

C2. gh is unavailable when GitHub creation was requested or could be offered
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

  gh CLI not found. Install it from https://cli.github.com/ and run `gh auth login` to add a GitHub remote.
  Continuing with local initialization only.

C3. gh is installed but unauthenticated
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

  gh CLI is not authenticated. Run `gh auth login` to add a GitHub remote.
  Continuing with local initialization only.

C4. GitHub creation was explicitly requested
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

Any of these expresses explicit creation intent and skips the consent prompt:
  --yes
  --push
  --repo-name <NAME>
  --repo-owner <OWNER>
  --repo-visibility <VISIBILITY>

C5. GitHub creation was not explicitly requested and gh is ready
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

Prompt, default No:

  ? Create a GitHub repository for "<REPO_PATH>"?

      Yes
    > No                                                        [default]

If No:
  - stay local-only;
  - continue to the initial-commit choice.

If Yes:
  - continue to GitHub owner, repository name, and visibility selection.

If Ctrl+C after git init:

  Bootstrap cancelled. A local git repository has been initialized but setup didn't complete. Run `entire enable` again to continue.


D. GitHub owner selection
-------------------------

D1. Organization lookup fails
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

The failure is non-fatal. Output:

  Warning: could not list organizations (<ERROR>). Only your user account is available.

D2. Only the current user is available, or --yes is active
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

No owner picker. Output:

    Using GitHub owner: <CURRENT_GITHUB_USER>

D3. Multiple owners are available and no owner flag was supplied
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

Prompt:

  ? Choose the GitHub owner for the new repository

    > <CURRENT_GITHUB_USER>                                    [default]
      <ORGANIZATION_1>
      <ORGANIZATION_2>
      ...

Ctrl+C after git init produces the bootstrap-cancelled output shown above.

D4. --repo-owner <OWNER>
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

No owner picker. The supplied owner is accepted even if it was not returned by
GitHub's known-owner query; gh may reject it later.


E. GitHub repository name
-------------------------

The suggested name is the current folder basename converted to a GitHub-safe
slug. Invalid characters become hyphens, repeated hyphens collapse, leading and
trailing hyphens/periods are removed, and an empty result becomes "my-repo".

E1. Interactive name prompt
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

  ? Repository name
    Press enter to use "<SUGGESTED_NAME>"
    <USER_INPUT>

Press Enter with empty input to accept <SUGGESTED_NAME>.

Validation failures print one of:

  Invalid name: name is required
  Invalid name: name must be at most 100 characters
  Invalid name: name must not contain '/' (pass --repo-owner separately)
  Invalid name: name cannot be '.' or '..'
  Invalid name: name may only contain letters, digits, '.', '-', '_'

After a validation failure, the repository-name prompt repeats.

If availability lookup says the name already exists:

  <OWNER>/<NAME> already exists on GitHub. Pick a different name.

Then the prompt repeats.

If availability lookup itself fails:

  Warning: could not check if <OWNER>/<NAME> already exists (<ERROR>). Proceeding; gh will error out if it is taken.

The flow then accepts the name.

E2. --repo-name <NAME>
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

No prompt. The name is validated and checked. If it exists:

  Error: repository <OWNER>/<NAME> already exists on GitHub

If checking fails:

  Warning: could not check if <OWNER>/<NAME> already exists (<ERROR>).

E3. --yes and the suggested name exists
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

With a TTY:

    <OWNER>/<SUGGESTED_NAME> already exists on GitHub.

Then the interactive repository-name prompt appears.

Without a TTY:

  Error: repository <OWNER>/<SUGGESTED_NAME> already exists on GitHub (use --repo-name to specify a different name)


F. Repository visibility
-------------------------

Prompt for a user-owned repository:

  ? Repository visibility

    > Private                                                   [default]
      Public

Prompt for an organization-owned repository:

  ? Repository visibility

    > Private                                                   [default]
      Public
      Internal

--yes defaults to private without prompting.
--repo-visibility skips the prompt.

Invalid supplied visibility:

  Error: invalid visibility "<VALUE>": must be one of public, private, internal

Internal visibility with a personal owner:

  Error: visibility 'internal' is only available for organization repositories


G. Initial commit choice
------------------------

This picker appears on the custom path unless the decision came from --yes,
--initial-commit-message, --skip-initial-commit, or a non-interactive default.

Prompt:

  ? Initial commit

    > Commit with default message "Initial commit"              [default]
      Customize message...
      Skip — I'll commit manually later

G1. Default commit
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

Commit with message:

  Initial commit

G2. Customize message
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

Prompt:

  ? Initial commit message
    Initial commit                                               [initial value]

An empty or whitespace-only result falls back to "Initial commit".

G3. Skip
~~~~~~~~

No identity or push prompt is needed when the flow is local-only. Final output
after Entire setup:

  Skipped initial commit. When you're ready:
    git add -A && git commit -m "Initial commit"

  Done.

If a GitHub repository was also requested:

  Creating GitHub repository
    ✓ Created <OWNER/REPO> (<VISIBILITY>)
      https://github.com/<OWNER/REPO>

    Skipped initial commit. When you're ready:
      git add -A && git commit -m "Initial commit"
      git push -u origin HEAD

  Done.


H. Git identity
---------------

Identity resolution happens when an initial commit will be created.

H1. Both git user.name and user.email already exist
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

No output and no prompt.

H2. Missing values are successfully sourced from gh
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

  Using git identity: <NAME> <<EMAIL>>

Missing GitHub email can become:

  <GITHUB_NUMERIC_ID>+<LOGIN>@users.noreply.github.com

H3. One or both values remain missing
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

Show only the missing field or fields:

  ? Git user.name
    <USER_INPUT>

  ? Git user.email
    <USER_INPUT>

The values are written to local repository config only.

Ctrl+C after git init:

  Bootstrap cancelled. A local git repository has been initialized but setup didn't complete. Run `entire enable` again to continue.


I. Initial push consent
-----------------------

This question is relevant only when:
  - a GitHub repository will be created; and
  - an initial commit will be attempted; and
  - push was not already accepted by the GitHub preset, --yes, or --push.

Prompt, default No:

  ? Push the initial commit to "<OWNER/REPO>"?

      Yes
    > No                                                        [default]

If Ctrl+C after git init:

  Bootstrap cancelled. A local git repository has been initialized but setup didn't complete. Run `entire enable` again to continue.

If No, the GitHub repository is created and origin is configured, but nothing is
published. Final output:

  Creating GitHub repository
    ✓ Created initial commit
    ✓ Created <OWNER/REPO> (<VISIBILITY>)
      https://github.com/<OWNER/REPO>

    Skipped push — nothing was published. When you're ready:
      git push -u origin HEAD

  Done.

If Yes:

  Publishing to GitHub
    ✓ Created initial commit
    ✓ Created <OWNER/REPO> (<VISIBILITY>)
      https://github.com/<OWNER/REPO>
    ✓ Pushed initial commit to origin

  Done.


J. Transition from bootstrap to Entire setup
---------------------------------------------

After all pre-setup bootstrap decisions are collected:

  Enabling Entire

The command then follows the repository setup router below. Bootstrap suppresses
that setup path's standalone "Ready." and empty-repository hint. If Entire setup
fails, commit/GitHub creation/push finalization does not run.


REPOSITORY SETUP ROUTING
========================

Once a git worktree exists, the command selects exactly one of these routes:

1. --agent <NAME> was supplied

   Run TARGETED AGENT SETUP.
   This skips the multi-agent selection picker and does not remove hooks for any
   other installed agent.

2. Entire settings already exist in either settings scope

   Run CONFIGURED REPOSITORY ENABLE.

3. No Entire settings exist yet

   Run FRESH REPOSITORY INTERACTIVE SETUP.


FRESH REPOSITORY INTERACTIVE SETUP
==================================

Step 1. Agent detection announcement
------------------------------------

The first setup checks detected agents before showing the picker.

Exactly one detected built-in agent:

  Detected agent: <AGENT_DISPLAY_NAME>

Multiple detected agents:

  Detected multiple agents: <AGENT_1>, <AGENT_2>, <AGENT_3>

Detected built-in agents are preselected in the picker. Detected external agents
are shown but are not preselected.

No announcement appears when:
  - no agent is detected;
  - --yes supplies automatic selection;
  - installed agent hooks make this a re-run-style selection.


Step 2. Agent selection prompt
------------------------------

Prompt:

  ? Select the agents you want to use
    Use space to select, enter to confirm.

    [ ] Claude Code
    [ ] Codex
    [ ] Copilot CLI
    [ ] Cursor
    [ ] Factory AI Droid
    [ ] Gemini CLI
    [ ] OpenCode
    [ ] Pi
    [ ] <EXTERNAL_AGENT_DISPLAY_NAME>
    ...

Preselection rules:
  - first run: detected built-in agents are checked;
  - re-run with installed hooks: installed agents are checked;
  - external agents are available but not auto-checked on first run.

Submitting no agents keeps the form open with validation text:

  please select at least one agent

After confirmation:

    Selected agents: <AGENT_1>, <AGENT_2>, <AGENT_3>

If the agent form is aborted, setup exits with an agent-selection error:

  Error: agent selection failed: agent selection cancelled: <FORM_ERROR>

--yes behavior:
  - no picker;
  - all available hook-capable, non-test agents are selected;
  - the "Selected agents" summary still prints.

Non-interactive behavior without --yes:
  - if detected agents exist, use them without a picker;
  - otherwise use Claude Code, the default, and print:

      Agent: Claude Code (use --agent to change)


Step 3. Remove hooks for deselected previously active agents
------------------------------------------------------------

For each previously installed agent that is not selected:

  Removed <AGENT_DISPLAY_NAME> hooks

A failure ends setup with:

  Error: failed to clean up deselected agents: <ERROR>


Step 4. Install selected agent hooks
------------------------------------

Hooks are installed for each selected agent. This loop is normally silent until
the aggregate project status later. A failure ends setup:

  Error: failed to setup <AGENT_DISPLAY_NAME> hooks: <ERROR>

If --search-skill was supplied, each selected agent may print one of:

    ✓ Installed <AGENT_DISPLAY_NAME> search skill
      <RELATIVE_SKILL_PATH>

    ✓ Updated <AGENT_DISPLAY_NAME> search skill
      <RELATIVE_SKILL_PATH>

    Skipped <AGENT_DISPLAY_NAME> search skill (unmanaged file exists)
      <RELATIVE_SKILL_PATH>

    Search skill is not supported for <AGENT_DISPLAY_NAME>

    Search skill already installed for <AGENT_DISPLAY_NAME>
      <RELATIVE_SKILL_PATH>

If --agent-help-skill was supplied, each selected agent may print one of:

    ✓ Installed <AGENT_DISPLAY_NAME> agent-help skill
      <RELATIVE_SKILL_PATH>

    ✓ Updated <AGENT_DISPLAY_NAME> agent-help skill
      <RELATIVE_SKILL_PATH>

    Skipped <AGENT_DISPLAY_NAME> agent-help skill (unmanaged file exists)
      <RELATIVE_SKILL_PATH>

    Agent-help skill is not supported for <AGENT_DISPLAY_NAME>
      <AGENT_DISPLAY_NAME> discovers entire via `entire agent-help` (passive — no skill file needed)

    Agent-help skill already installed for <AGENT_DISPLAY_NAME>
      <RELATIVE_SKILL_PATH>

Selecting an external agent causes the resulting settings to enable external
agent discovery.


Step 5. Checkpoint storage selection
------------------------------------

This prompt appears only when all are true:
  - this is the first Entire setup;
  - --checkpoint-backend was not supplied;
  - --yes was not supplied;
  - interactive prompting is available;
  - ENTIRE_CHECKPOINTS_PRIMARY is not set.

Prompt:

  ? Checkpoint storage
    How Entire stores committed session checkpoints in your repo.

    > Refs — one git ref per checkpoint (recommended)            [default]
      Branch — one shared branch, entire/checkpoints/v1

The selected canonical setting is:
  Refs   -> git-refs
  Branch -> git-branch

If the picker itself is cancelled without cancelling the command context:

  Checkpoint storage selection cancelled.
  Using the recommended git-refs checkpoint storage.

The setup continues with git-refs.

If the command context was cancelled:

  Checkpoint storage selection cancelled.
  Error: checkpoint storage selection: context canceled

The setup stops.

--yes or non-interactive first setup:
  - no checkpoint prompt;
  - git-refs is selected silently.

ENTIRE_CHECKPOINTS_PRIMARY set:
  - no checkpoint prompt;
  - no checkpoint backend is written because the environment override owns the
    effective backend.


Step 6. Choose and write the settings target
--------------------------------------------

First run normally writes:

  .entire/settings.json

If project settings already exist and setup chooses the local override by
default:

  Info: Project settings exist. Saving to settings.local.json instead.
    Use --project to update the project settings file.

Explicit scope:
  --project -> .entire/settings.json
  --local   -> .entire/settings.local.json


Step 7. Install Entire git hooks
--------------------------------

Normal success output:

    ✓ Installed hooks
    ✓ Configured project
      .entire/settings.json

Or:

    ✓ Installed hooks
    ✓ Configured project
      .entire/settings.local.json

If an external git-hook manager is detected, advisory output may appear before
"✓ Installed hooks".

For a manager such as Husky that overwrites hooks:

  Warning: <HOOK_MANAGER> detected (<CONFIG_PATH>)

    <HOOK_MANAGER> may overwrite hooks installed by Entire on npm install.
    To make Entire hooks permanent, add these lines to your <HOOK_MANAGER> hook files:

      <HOOK_DIRECTORY>prepare-commit-msg:
        <ENTIRE_PREPARE_COMMIT_MSG_COMMAND>

      <HOOK_DIRECTORY>commit-msg:
        <ENTIRE_COMMIT_MSG_COMMAND>

      <HOOK_DIRECTORY>post-commit:
        <ENTIRE_POST_COMMIT_COMMAND>

      <HOOK_DIRECTORY>pre-push:
        <ENTIRE_PRE_PUSH_COMMAND>

For a non-overwriting manager:

  Note: <HOOK_MANAGER> detected (<CONFIG_PATH>)

    If <HOOK_MANAGER> reinstalls hooks, run 'entire enable' to restore Entire's hooks.


Step 8. Optional Vercel handling
--------------------------------

Vercel is considered detected when any of these exists:
  vercel.json
  .vercel
  vercel.ts

The Vercel question is skipped when:
  - none of those markers exists;
  - the target settings already have "vercel": true;
  - vercel.json already disables deployment for entire/**, in which case the
    settings are synchronized automatically;
  - filesystem checks fail, in which case a note is printed;
  - the run cannot prompt, in which case a follow-up instruction is printed.

If vercel.json already contains the expected deployment block:

  ✓ Updated <CONFIG> to manage Vercel deployment blocking on `entire/**`

If a Vercel marker cannot be checked:

  Note: Skipping Vercel deployment update: could not check vercel.json: <ERROR>

Or:

  Note: Skipping Vercel deployment update: could not check <PATH>: <ERROR>

If Vercel is detected but prompting is unavailable:

  Note: Vercel detected. Run `entire configure` interactively to disable deployments for `entire/**` branches.

Interactive prompt, default Yes:

  ? Disable Vercel deployments for Entire metadata branch?
    This automatically creates a vercel.json in the Entire metadata branch.

    > Yes                                                       [default]
      No

If No:
  - no Vercel setting is changed;
  - no Vercel success line is printed.

If Yes:

  ✓ Updated <CONFIG> to block Vercel deploys of Entire metadata branch

With --yes:
  - no Vercel prompt;
  - Yes is selected automatically when Vercel is detected and not configured.


Step 9. Telemetry consent
-------------------------

This prompt appears only when:
  - --yes was not supplied;
  - --telemetry=false was not supplied;
  - telemetry is not already recorded in settings;
  - ENTIRE_TELEMETRY_OPTOUT is not set.

Prompt, default Yes:

  ? Help improve Entire CLI?
    Share anonymous usage data. No code or personal info collected.

    > Yes                                                       [default]
      No

Yes writes telemetry=true.
No writes telemetry=false.

No prompt and telemetry=false when:
  --telemetry=false
  ENTIRE_TELEMETRY_OPTOUT is non-empty

With --yes:
  - no prompt;
  - telemetry defaults to true when it was unset;
  - an existing telemetry value is preserved;
  - --telemetry=false and ENTIRE_TELEMETRY_OPTOUT still force false.

A form error ends setup:

  Error: telemetry consent: telemetry prompt: <FORM_ERROR>


Step 10. Ensure checkpoint strategy metadata
--------------------------------------------

This is normally silent. Failure ends setup:

  Error: failed to setup strategy: <ERROR>

When checkpoint_remote is configured, this explicit enable may fetch and heal a
missing primary metadata ref.


Step 11. Optional import of pre-existing agent history
------------------------------------------------------

This offer appears only when:
  - this is the first Entire enable;
  - one or more selected agents has a registered importer;
  - at least one session for this repository was discovered within the last 30
    days.

No eligible sessions:
  - no prompt;
  - no import output.

Non-interactive without --yes:

  Found importable history for 1 agent. Run 'entire import <agent>' to import it.

Or:

  Found importable history for <N> agents. Run 'entire import <agent>' to import it.

--yes:
  - no prompt;
  - every eligible agent is imported automatically.

Step 11A. Exactly one eligible agent
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

Prompt, default Skip:

  ? Import existing <AGENT_DISPLAY_NAME> sessions into Entire? (optional)
    <N> sessions from the last 30 days. Enter to confirm.

      Import
    > Skip                                                      [default]

For exactly one session, the description is:

    1 session from the last 30 days. Enter to confirm.

If Skip:
  - no import occurs;
  - setup continues.

If Import, success output:

  Imported <TURNS_IMPORTED> turn(s) from <SESSIONS_SCANNED> session(s) (<TURNS_ALREADY_IMPORTED> already imported).

Step 11B. Multiple eligible agents
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

Prompt with nothing preselected:

  ? Import existing sessions into Entire? (optional)
    Space to select, enter to confirm. Select none to skip.

    [ ] <AGENT_1>  (<N> sessions, last 30 days)
    [ ] <AGENT_2>  (<N> sessions, last 30 days)
    [ ] <AGENT_3>  (1 session, last 30 days)
    ...

Each selected agent prints:

  Imported <TURNS_IMPORTED> turn(s) from <SESSIONS_SCANNED> session(s) (<TURNS_ALREADY_IMPORTED> already imported).

Confirming an empty selection skips import.

Step 11C. Import prompt cancellation
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

For either import form:

  Import cancelled.

Import is skipped and setup continues.

Step 11D. Best-effort import failures
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

A prompt/UI failure that is not a normal cancellation:

  Note: could not show import prompt: <ERROR>

Repository open failure:

  Note: could not import agent history: <ERROR>

Checkpoint policy prevents imported checkpoint data:

  Note: skipping agent history import: <ERROR>

Per-agent import failure:

  Note: could not import <AGENT_DISPLAY_NAME> history: <ERROR>

Remaining selected agents continue importing.

Step 11E. Logged-out local-only import notice
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

When at least one turn was imported or already present and Entire is not logged
in:

  Note:

# `entire enable`: complete potential interactive flow and output map

```text
DOCUMENT SCOPE
==============

This is a source-derived map of every prompt and user-visible step reachable from
`entire enable`, including first-time setup, an already-configured repository,
non-git-directory bootstrap, GitHub bootstrap, targeted --agent setup, optional
skills, Vercel handling, telemetry, history import, cancellation, and completion.

Primary source paths:
  cmd/entire/cli/setup.go
  cmd/entire/cli/setup_github.go
  cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint_backend.go
  cmd/entire/cli/setup_import.go
  cmd/entire/cli/setup_search_skill.go
  cmd/entire/cli/setup_agent_help_skill.go
  cmd/entire/cli/import_sync_notice.go
  cmd/entire/cli/strategy/hook_managers.go

Notation used below:
  <...>                 dynamic value
  [condition]           branch condition; not literal CLI output
  [default: ...]        initial selection
  [selected]            preselected multi-select option
  [optional output]     appears only when the stated condition is true
  [silent]              no user-visible output for that step
  →                     next step or branch

The normal TUI is rendered by huh and may redraw options in place. The text below
lists the stable titles, descriptions, labels, defaults, choices, and follow-up
output rather than terminal cursor-control sequences. When ACCESSIBLE is set,
huh renders equivalent numbered/static prompts and may omit descriptions.


TOP-LEVEL ROUTING
=================

$ entire enable [flags]

1. Validate --checkpoint-backend, if explicitly supplied.

   Accepted user-facing values:
     refs
     branch

   Accepted canonical values:
     git-refs
     git-branch

   Invalid input exits before repository bootstrap or hook installation:
     Error: invalid --checkpoint-backend: <validation error>

2. Determine whether the current directory is in a git worktree.

   [inside a git worktree]
     → Skip NON-GIT-DIRECTORY BOOTSTRAP.
     → Continue to ENABLE ROUTING INSIDE A GIT REPOSITORY.

   [not inside a git worktree]
     → Continue to NON-GIT-DIRECTORY BOOTSTRAP.

3. Validate settings-scope flags.

   [both --local and --project]
     Error: cannot specify both --project and --local

4. Discover built-in and external agent integrations.

5. Route by command state and flags.

   [--agent <name> supplied]
     → TARGETED --agent FLOW.

   [Entire has any existing setup/settings]
     → ALREADY-CONFIGURED REPOSITORY FLOW.

   [Entire has no existing setup/settings]
     → FIRST-TIME SETUP FLOW.

6. After a successful enable, report the enabled repository to the Entire API and
   probe trail enablement.

   This final reporting step is best-effort and completely silent for all results:
     no origin remote
     unsupported forge
     not logged in
     network failure
     API report failure
     trails probe failure
     local cache write failure


NON-GIT-DIRECTORY BOOTSTRAP
===========================

The bootstrap runs before agent setup. It first initializes git and gathers all
GitHub/commit decisions. Agent setup then runs. The initial commit/GitHub creation
happens last so the commit includes files created by Entire setup.

A. Bare interactive bootstrap: combined setup picker
----------------------------------------------------

This one-step preset picker is shown only when all of these are true:
  interactive prompting is available
  --yes was not passed
  --init-repo was not passed
  --no-init-repo was not passed
  --no-github was not passed
  no --repo-name/--repo-owner/--repo-visibility flag was passed
  --push was not passed
  --initial-commit-message was not passed
  --skip-initial-commit was not passed

Prompt:
  No git repository in "<absolute-current-directory>". Set one up?

Options:
  > Yes, with one initial commit (recommended)
    [default]

    Yes, plus a private GitHub repository (pushed)
    [shown only when the gh CLI is installed and authenticated]

    Yes, customize...

    No

A1. Choose "No"
  No filesystem changes are made.

  Not a git repository. Please run 'entire enable' from within a git repository, or pass --init-repo to initialize one here.

A2. Press Ctrl+C in this combined picker
  Treated like choosing "No".
  No filesystem changes are made.

  Not a git repository. Please run 'entire enable' from within a git repository, or pass --init-repo to initialize one here.

A3. Choose "Yes, with one initial commit (recommended)"
  Implied decisions:
    initialize git
    do not create a GitHub repository
    create one initial commit
    use commit message "Initial commit"

  Continue with:

  Setting up git repository
    ✓ Initialized empty git repository

  [git identity is already configured]
    [no identity prompt or output]

  [git identity is missing but can be obtained from authenticated gh]
    Using git identity: <name> <<email>>

  [git identity still has missing values]
    → GIT IDENTITY PROMPTS

  Enabling Entire

  → FIRST-TIME SETUP FLOW
  → BOOTSTRAP FINALIZATION: LOCAL INITIAL COMMIT

A4. Choose "Yes, plus a private GitHub repository (pushed)"
  This option is present only when gh is installed and authenticated.

  Implied decisions:
    initialize git
    create GitHub repository
    owner = authenticated GitHub user
    name = slugified current folder name
    visibility = private
    create initial commit with "Initial commit"
    push initial commit

  Continue with:

  Setting up git repository
    ✓ Initialized empty git repository
    Using GitHub owner: <current-user>

  [suggested repository name is available]
    [no repository-name prompt]

  [suggested repository name already exists and interactive prompting is available]
    <owner>/<suggested-name> already exists on GitHub.
    → REPOSITORY NAME PROMPT

  [git identity is already configured]
    [no identity prompt or output]

  [git identity is sourced from gh]
    Using git identity: <name> <<email>>

  [git identity remains incomplete]
    → GIT IDENTITY PROMPTS

  Enabling Entire

  → FIRST-TIME SETUP FLOW
  → BOOTSTRAP FINALIZATION: CREATE AND PUSH GITHUB REPOSITORY

A5. Choose "Yes, customize..."
  Continue with:

  Setting up git repository
    ✓ Initialized empty git repository

  → CUSTOM GITHUB REPOSITORY CONSENT
  → INITIAL COMMIT PROMPT
  → GIT IDENTITY PROMPTS, if a commit will be created
  → PUSH CONFIRMATION, if GitHub creation and a commit were selected
  → FIRST-TIME SETUP FLOW
  → matching BOOTSTRAP FINALIZATION branch


B. Granular initialization consent
----------------------------------

The combined picker is skipped when flags already express any granular bootstrap
choice. If initialization itself was not answered by --init-repo, --no-init-repo,
or --yes, this confirmation is shown:

Prompt:
  Warning: Not a git repository. Initialize a new one in "<absolute-current-directory>"?

Default:
  No

Choices:
  Yes
  No

B1. Choose No or cancel
  Not a git repository. Please run 'entire enable' from within a git repository, or pass --init-repo to initialize one here.

B2. Choose Yes

  Setting up git repository
    ✓ Initialized empty git repository

  → Continue through the custom/flag-resolved bootstrap decisions.

B3. --no-init-repo
  No prompt.

  Not a git repository. Please run 'entire enable' from within a git repository, or pass --init-repo to initialize one here.

B4. --init-repo or --yes
  Initialization is accepted without prompting.

  Setting up git repository
    ✓ Initialized empty git repository


CUSTOM GITHUB REPOSITORY CONSENT
================================

Reached after initialization when using custom bootstrap choices, unless
--no-github explicitly disables remote creation.

1. gh CLI missing when GitHub creation was explicitly requested or would be offered:

   gh CLI not found. Install it from https://cli.github.com/ and run `gh auth login` to add a GitHub remote.
   Continuing with local initialization only.

   → No GitHub details or push prompts.

2. gh CLI installed but not authenticated:

   gh CLI is not authenticated. Run `gh auth login` to add a GitHub remote.
   Continuing with local initialization only.

   → No GitHub details or push prompts.

3. GitHub creation explicitly requested by any of these:
     --yes
     --push
     --repo-name
     --repo-owner
     --repo-visibility

   No create-repository confirmation is shown.
   → GITHUB OWNER RESOLUTION.

4. GitHub creation not explicitly requested, gh is ready, and prompting is interactive:

   Prompt:
     Create a GitHub repository for "<absolute-current-directory>"?

   Default:
     No

   Choices:
     Yes
     No

   [No]
     → Skip GitHub details and push.

   [Yes]
     → GITHUB OWNER RESOLUTION.

5. Ctrl+C in this prompt after git init:

   Bootstrap cancelled. A local git repository has been initialized but setup didn't complete. Run `entire enable` again to continue.


GITHUB OWNER RESOLUTION
=======================

1. Query authenticated GitHub user and organizations.

2. If organizations cannot be listed:

   Warning: could not list organizations (<error>). Only your user account is available.

3. If --repo-owner was passed:
   Use it without prompting, even if it is not in the enumerated owner list.

4. If only the authenticated user is available, or --yes was passed:

   Using GitHub owner: <current-user>

5. If multiple owners are available and prompting is interactive:

   Prompt:
     Choose the GitHub owner for the new repository

   Options:
     > <current-user>                  [default]
       <organization-1>
       <organization-2>
       ...

6. Ctrl+C after git init:

   Bootstrap cancelled. A local git repository has been initialized but setup didn't complete. Run `entire enable` again to continue.


REPOSITORY NAME RESOLUTION
==========================

Suggested name:
  slugified basename of <absolute-current-directory>

Slug rules:
  letters/digits preserved
  '-', '_', and '.' preserved
  all other characters become '-'
  repeated '-' collapsed
  leading/trailing '-' and '.' trimmed
  empty result becomes "my-repo"

1. --repo-name <name>

   No prompt if valid and available.

     name is required

     name must not contain '/' (pass --repo-owner separately)
     name cannot be '.' or '..'
     name may only contain letters, digits, '.', '-', '_'

   If availability cannot be checked:
     Warning: could not check if <owner>/<name> already exists (<error>).

   If it exists:
     Error: repository <owner>/<name> already exists on GitHub

2. --yes and suggested name is available
   Use suggested name silently.

3. --yes and availability check fails

   Warning: could not check if <owner>/<suggested-name> already exists (<error>).

   Continue with the suggested name and let gh report any later conflict.

     <typed-name-or-empty-for-suggestion>

     Invalid name: <validation error>

   Existing repository loops with:
     <owner>/<name> already exists on GitHub. Pick a different name.

   Availability-check failure accepts the name with:
     Warning: could not check if <owner>/<name> already exists (<error>). Proceeding; gh will error out if it is taken.

In explicit-target mode, `runAttach` still calls `saveAttachSessionState`, which unconditionally sets `state.LastCheckpointID = checkpointID` (the server-minted, commit-SHA-bound review checkpoint) and, if `BaseCommit` was empty, sets it to the current HEAD. `LastCheckpointID`/`BaseCommit` are also read by `handleAmendCommitMsg` (prepare-commit-msg hook) to auto-restore an `Entire-Checkpoint` trailer on a later `git commit --amend` of the same base commit, and by the resume picker. Since the explicit-target checkpoint is deliberately *not* meant to be trailer-linked (it's bound via `commit_sha` metadata, not a trailer), this can cause a later unrelated amend to silently inject the review-provenance checkpoint ID as the code checkpoint trailer, or make `session resume`/`sessions` misreport the session's checkpoint linkage.

entire trail checkout — Check out a trail's branch
Check out the branch of a trail.

The trail may be given as the first argument or via --trail, as a number, id, or
branch. Without one, the trail for the current branch is used. The trail's branch
is checked out, fetching it from origin first when it only exists there.

With --worktree, the branch is checked out into a git worktree under
.entire/worktrees at the repo root instead of switching this checkout, and the
command prints a cd command for the new worktree. Gitignored files matching
.worktreeinclude patterns are copied into the worktree. When stdout is not a
terminal, only the worktree path is printed, so scripts can use
cd "$(entire trail checkout <trail> --worktree)".

This must be run from within a clone of the repository the trail belongs to; the
trail is looked up against that repository's origin remote.

Current repo: gh/entireio/cli  (auto-detected from origin; pass --repo only for a DIFFERENT repo)

Flags:
  -f, --force          Skip the prompt before fetching a remote-only branch
      --trail string   Trail to check out (number, id, or branch; defaults to the current branch's trail)
      --worktree       Check out the trail branch in a worktree under .entire/worktrees instead of switching this checkout

Inherited flags:
      --repo string   Target repository as forge/owner/repo (e.g. gh/acme/app) or a clone URL; defaults to the origin remote

if fetchErr != nil {

			slog.String("error", fetchErr.Error()))

```
When `refreshCheckpoint` fails inside `ensureExplicitCheckpointFreshness` (network blip, auth failure, remote misconfig), this treats the checkpoint as "not present" and lets the caller proceed to write a brand-new checkpoint under the caller-supplied ID. `FetchCheckpointRef`'s own doc says a fetch failure is indistinguishable from "ref doesn't exist" ("the caller treats a fetch failure as 'checkpoint not found'"), so a transient fetch error on a retry — exactly the scenario this function exists to guard against per its own docstring — silently takes the risky path and can rebuild the ID as an orphan that clobbers the original checkpoint on push. Compare with the sibling `ensureCheckpointAvailable`, which on the same fetch failure falls through to `missingCheckpointError` and refuses rather than assuming safety. This branch should likewise propagate the fetch error instead of returning `(repo, false, nil)`.
